{{short description|Event in which two or more people assemble, planned in advance to facilitate discussion}}
{{About|meetings in general|meetings in organizations that use parliamentary procedure|Meeting (parliamentary procedure)|multi-event athletic competitions|Track and field#Meetings|other uses}}
[[File:Sitzung von Wiki Loves Broadcast im Kontor Hamburg.jpg|thumb|Hybrid meeting: People meet in person and connect digitally with others]]

A '''meeting''' is when two or more [[Homo sapiens|people]] come together to discuss one or more topics, often in a formal or business setting, but meetings also occur in a variety of other environments. Meetings can be used as form of [[group decision-making]] and as a setting for sharing of [[Business intelligence|information]]<ref>Dima Eremin (June 27, 2024)
·[https://www.bluedothq.com/blog/business-meeting-most-common-types-and-how-to-run-it-effectively Business Meeting: Most Common Types And How To Run It Effectively] bluedothq</ref> or [[Intelligence (information)|intelligence]].

== Definition ==

A meeting refers to a gathering with a specific agenda and not just mere gathering of people casually talking to each other.<ref name="pi"/> Meetings may occur face-to-face or virtually, as mediated by communications technology, such as a [[conference call|telephone conference call]], a [[Skype|skyped conference call]] or a [[videoconferencing|videoconference]]. Merriam-Webster dictionary defines a meeting as "an act or process of coming together" - for example "as [...] an assembly for a common purpose [...]".<ref name="pu">[http://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/meeting Meeting – Definition and More from the Free Merriam-Webster Dictionary]. (n.d.). Dictionary and Thesaurus – Merriam-Webster Online. Retrieved 2016-02-04.</ref>

[[Meeting planner]]s and other meeting [[professional]]s may use the term "meeting" to denote an event booked at a hotel, [[convention center]] or any other venue dedicated to such gatherings.<ref name="pi">[http://www.bls.gov/oco/ocos298.htm Meeting and Convention Planners]. (2009, December 17). [[U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics]]. Retrieved April 21, 2010.</ref><ref>
{{cite book
| last1                 = Montgomery
| first1                = Rhonda J.
| last2                 = Strick
| first2                = Sandra K.
| title                 = Meetings, Conventions, and Expositions: An Introduction to the Industry
| url                   = https://books.google.com/books?id=bgWRbYjTLVsC
| location              = New York
| publisher             = [[John Wiley & Sons|Wiley]]
| date      = 1994
| isbn                  = 9780471284390
| access-date            = 2016-02-04
}}
</ref>

Anthropologist Helen B. Schwartzman defines a meeting as "a communicative event involving three or more people who agree to assemble for a purpose ostensibly related to the functioning of an organization or group."<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|last=Schwartzman|first=Helen B.|title=The Meeting : Gatherings in Organizations and Communities|date=1989|publisher=Springer US|isbn=978-1-4899-0885-8|pages=7|oclc=859586941}}</ref> For her, meetings are characterized by "multiparty talk that is episodic in nature, and participants either develop or use specific conventions for regulating this talk."<ref name=":0" />

Russia also shares [[Maritime boundary|maritime boundaries]] with Japan and the United States. Russia also shares borders with the two [[partially recognized states|partially recognised]] breakaway states of [[South Ossetia]] and [[Abkhazia]] that it occupies in Georgia.}} With a population of over 140 million, Russia is the [[List of European countries by population|most populous country in Europe]] and the [[List of countries and dependencies by population|ninth-most populous in the world]]. It is a [[Urbanization by sovereign state|highly urbanised]] country, with sixteen of its urban areas having more than 1 million inhabitants. ([[Federal Assembly (Russia)|Federal Assembly]]: [[Federation Council (Russia)|Federation Council]], [[State Duma]]) | executive = [[Prime Minister of Russia|Prime Minister]]-led [[Government of Russia|Government]] | courts = [[Judiciary of Russia|Judiciary]] ([[Constitutional Court of Russia|Constitutional Court]], [[Supreme Court of Russia|Supreme Court]]) | federalism = Federation | electoral_college = No | number_entrenchments = 9 | date_legislature = [[1st State Duma|12 December 1993]] | date_first_executive = [[Second inauguration of Boris Yeltsin|9 August 1996]] | date_first_court = | date_repealed = | number_amendments = 4 (plus 11 alternations on [[Federal subjects of Russia|Federal subjects]]) | date_last_amended = 4 July 2020 | location_of_document = [[Moscow Kremlin|Kremlin]], [[Moscow]] | commissioned = [[Constitutional Conference of Russia|Constitutional Conference]] | writer = | signers = [[1993 Russian constitutional referendum|Constitutional referendum]] by the [[Citizenship of Russia|citizens of Russia]] | media_type = | supersedes = [[Russian Constitution of 1978|Constitution of the RSFSR]] |wikisource = Constitution of Russia }} {{Politics of Russia}} The '''Constitution of the Russian Federation''' ({{Langx|ru|Конституция Российской Федерации|translit=Konstitutsiya Rossiyskoy Federatsii}}) was adopted by national referendum on 12 December 1993 and enacted on 25 December 1993.https://legislationline.org/sites/default/files/2025-02/CONSTITUTION%20OF%20THE%20RUSSIAN%20FEDERATION.pdf The latest significant reform occurred in 2020, marked by extensive amendments that altered various sections, including presidential terms, social policies, and the role of Russian law over international ones. (See [[2020 amendments to the Constitution of Russia]]). [[Russia]]'s constitution came into force on 25 December 1993, at the moment of its official publication, and abolished the [[Soviet republic (system of government)|Soviet system of government]]. The 1993 Constitution is one of the longest-standing constitutions in Russian history, second only to the Soviet-era [[Russian Constitution of 1937|1937 Constitution]], which was in effect until 1978. [[File:Constitition of Russia (m book) 1.JPG|thumb|In [[miniature book]] version.]] The text was drafted by the [[Constitutional Conference of the Russian Federation|1993 Constitutional Conference]], which was attended by over 800 participants. [[Sergei Alexeyev]], [[Sergey Shakhray]], and sometimes [[Anatoly Sobchak]] are considered as the primary co-authors of the constitution. The text was inspired by [[Mikhail Speransky]]'s constitutional project and the current [[French constitution]].{{YouTube|93fQtQcb_wg|Sergey Shakhray - The Voice of Russia}} The [[United States Agency for International Development|USAID]]-funded lawyers also contributed to the development of the draft.{{cite web |title=USAID In Russia |url=https://www.usaid.gov/news-information/fact-sheets/usaid-russia |website=[[USAID]] |date=18 September 2012 |publisher=[[United States Agency for International Development]] |access-date=16 December 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201111222942/https://www.usaid.gov/news-information/fact-sheets/usaid-russia |archive-date=11 November 2020}} It replaced the previous [[Soviet Union|Soviet]]-era [[Russian Constitution of 1978|Constitution of 12 April 1978]], of the [[Russian SFSR|Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic]] (which had already been amended in April 1992 to reflect the dissolution of the Soviet Union and the [[Declaration of State Sovereignty of the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic|sovereignty of the Russian Federation]]), following the [[1993 Russian constitutional crisis]].
